lines.text: Camera Corrections is tiny. Lines nineteen to twenty two map each camera's name to its fix. Right now, all zero.
Line twenty eight returns the fix, or no change for a camera never calibrated.
The calibration op mode sets the tag, the parked spot, and a straight back-off from the tag, at zero point one five meters per second for four seconds.
Start, line eighty seven: the parked pose, composed with tag to parked inverted. Four point six, one, one eighty.
Then it backs off. Periodic adds a frame from each camera every loop, stops the robot at four seconds, and prints at four and a half.
Add frame, line one twenty one, starts with Tag Tracker's checks: a new frame, with our tag.
Lines one thirty six to one forty six get the measured pose, its age, and the rewound wheel pose.
Line one forty eight: the tag seen from the robot at capture. Zero point nine, zero, one eighty.
Lines one forty nine to one fifty one: expected, composed with measured inverse. The fix: three and a half millimeters, minus four point three, one degree.
Lines one fifty two to one fifty six add it to the sums, using sine and cosine for the angle. Then each sample is logged.
Print corrections averages the sums; line one seventy eight turns sine and cosine back into an angle. Paste the printed line into Camera Corrections.
From then on, line one thirty six in Tag Tracker fixes every photo from that camera. Under twenty photos? It warns instead.
